boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Rice's Station record (April 6, 1865) in the Appomattox Campaign [March-April 1865]. Sailor's Creek (VA093) and the April 6 High Bridge fight (VA095) are the same day. Army-wide returns, campaign-wide loss and prisoner totals, the April 9 paroles and the retreat as a whole are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads 'Corps' and the live field zero. claims.rationale: Formation lists and an earlier army-level figure; no count at Rice's Station. None is adopted as a matched opening strength; live zeros are not measured absence.

claims.value: The frozen and live results read Union victory. Gibbon says night ended the operations before his troops could drive in the pickets and the enemy was gone at daylight, retreating across the Appomattox at Farmville; Humphreys says Longstreet marched for Farmville as soon as night set in and crossed there; NPS says Longstreet withdrew over the High Bridge.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit. NPS's High Bridge route conflicts with Humphreys' and Gibbon's Farmville crossing for Longstreet's column (Humphreys sends Gordon and Mahone over High Bridge); not reconciled.

NPS/CWSAC (the live NPS page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Humphreys' The Virginia Campaign of ’64 and ’65 (1883) is an interested history by the commander of the Second Corps in this campaign, in the same author family as the registered From Gettysburg to the Rapidan; where it narrates his own corps it is a participant's account. It relies on the reports of Sheridan, Warren, Wright, Gibbon, Ewell and Fitzhugh Lee, on Confederate testimony before the Warren Court of Inquiry and on the returns, so it is not independent of those families. Lee's, Sheridan's, Bushrod Johnson's, Miles's, Gibbon's, Ewell's and Fitzhugh Lee's papers, printed in Official Records Series I, Volume XLVI, Part 1, are separate families of interested commanders' accounts; the volume is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
